newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: North Korean spy gets 15-year jail term in Seoul.
newsitem.headline: North Korean spy gets 15-year jail term in Seoul.

text.p: A North Korean spy who posed as a Filipino university professor in Seoul on Thursday was jailed for 15 years, escaping a death sentence demanded by state prosecutors.
Chung Su-il, 62, lied about his name, his age and nationality for more than a decade after arriving in South Korea in 1984 using forged documents.
An official at the Seoul District Criminal Court, who confirmed the sentencing, could give no details of whether Chung or the prosecution would appeal.
Under the alias Mohamad Ali Kanso, Chung taught history at Dankook University from 1990.

He kept his identity secret from his South Korean wife of eight years. She thought he was 11 years younger than he really was, and had no idea he was already married with three daughters in North Korea.
He was arrested at a Seoul hotel in July while faxing information to a Pyongyang agent in Beijing on the deployment of recently imported Apache helicopters and the test firing of self-propelled guns.
In reality, Chung worked for the external information research department of North Korea's ruling Workers' Party, and before beginning his spy career in Seoul, earned a master's degree in Lebanon.
The former professor of foreign studies at Pyongyang University gained Filipino nationality with fake papers.

During his trial, prosecutors quoted Chung as saying he apologised for "endangering the well-being of the people by engaging in an act of spying". He admitted passing on information to North Korea for a decade.
After his arrest, South Korea's spy-catching Agency for National Security Planning displayed poisoned needles, code books and other espionage paraphernalia seized from Chung.
South Korea has been technically at war with North Korea since their 1950-53 conflict ended with a truce rather than a peace agreement.
